questions.question_text: Which unit is more suitable for recording the area of a suburban park covering about $80\,000\text{ m}^{2}$?

options.why: Chose a region-sized unit that is too large for a suburban park.
Used a unit of length rather than a square unit for area.
Used a cubic unit for volume instead of a unit for land area.

questions.solution_text:
$80\,000\text{ m}^{2}=8\text{ ha}=0.08\text{ km}^{2}$.
Hectares give the more suitable-sized measure.

options.why: Divided by $1\,000$ instead of by $10\,000$ square metres per hectare.
Divided by $100$ instead of by $10\,000$ square metres per hectare.
Multiplied by $10$ instead of dividing by $10\,000$ to change to a larger unit.
Multiplied by $1\,000$ instead of by $10\,000$ square metres per hectare.
Multiplied by $100$, confusing hectares with the hectare-to-square-kilometre relationship.
Divided by $10\,000$ even though converting from hectares to the smaller square-metre unit requires multiplication.
Multiplied by $10$ instead of by $100$ hectares per square kilometre.
Multiplied by $1\,000$ instead of by $100$ hectares per square kilometre.
Divided by $100$ even though hectares are the smaller unit and the number should increase.
Compared $95$ with $1.1$ directly without converting them to the same unit.
Treated $1\text{ km}^{2}$ as $100$ ha but ignored the extra $0.1\text{ km}^{2}=10$ ha.
Missed that square kilometres and hectares are convertible area units.

questions.solution_text:
$1.1\text{ km}^{2}$
$=110\text{ ha}$
$110\text{ ha}>95\text{ ha}$
$1.1\text{ km}^{2}$ is larger.

questions.question_text:
A reserve joins parcels of $0.85\text{ km}^{2}$ and $40$ ha.
What is the total area in hectares?

options.why: Added $0.85$ directly to $40$ without converting square kilometres to hectares.
Converted $0.85\text{ km}^{2}$ to $8.5$ ha by multiplying by $10$ instead of $100$.
Treated $40$ ha as $4\,000$ ha before adding the correctly converted $85$ ha.
